remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. Abiquiú Notebooks notes inscriptions 1, 2, 4. Completed in New York on basis of Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence and O'Keeffe letter: "Walking down the hall of Columbia University Art Department, I heard mu*sic* [spring 1916]. Being curious, I opened the door and went in. The instructor was playing a low–toned record, asking the class to make a charcoal drawing from it. . . .*Drawing No. 14* is the one that I made at the time and it gave me an idea that I was very interested to follow –– the idea of lines like sounds" (*Some Memories of Drawings* [1988], unpaginated). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Thin black stripes run diagonally from the bottom left corner to the top right of the composition. A large, textured semicircular form fills much of the composition, extending from the bottom into the top third of the paper. Six dark gray, square shapes are distributed around the upper right portion of the image.
